original_formulation: Positive/internal/confining pressure radially or transversely compresses a metallic wire bundle, increases inter-wire normal force/friction, changes bending/torsional/axial stiffness.
scientific_purpose: Determine whether applying external positive fluid or mechanical confinement pressure to compress a metallic/NiTi wire bundle to modulate stiffness constitutes a novel mechanics principle.
kill_condition: Finding prior work applying transverse/radial confining pressure to multi-element bundles, or demonstrating that pressure acts as an experimental boundary condition rather than a novel constitutive mechanism.

papers_tested.paper_title: Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable
papers_tested.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/2017-Bending Mechanics of Cable Cores and Fillers in a Dynamic Submarine Cable.pdf
papers_tested.method: Analytical and finite element beam bending formulation
papers_tested.material_or_system: Dynamic submarine power cable with multi-component metallic cores and fillers
papers_tested.loading_mode: Cyclic bending under external radial contact pressure
papers_tested.model_used: Stick-slip friction beam mechanics with pressure-dependent normal force
papers_tested.experiment_used: Full-scale cable bending test rig with 0.2 MPa radial contact pressure
papers_tested.what_source_proves: Proves that external radial confining pressure directly increases inter-element normal force, delaying slip and modulating dynamic flexural rigidity.
papers_tested.what_source_does_not_prove: Applies a constant radial pressure rather than actively varying pressure as a dynamic control input on NiTi.

papers_tested.experiment_used: Universal testing machine with pressure regulator
papers_tested.what_source_proves: Proves positive pneumatic pressure modulates bending stiffness via normal confinement.
papers_tested.what_source_does_not_prove: Uses granular media instead of metallic NiTi wires.
